---
title: "Time passed"
description: "How OPDI gives the time from the first report of the track to each event (time_passed_s)."
---

## In one sentence

`time_passed_s` is the time from the track's `first_seen` event to the event,
in seconds.

## What it needs

The `first_seen` event of the track (see
[First seen and last seen](first-last-seen.qmd)) and the time of the event.

## How it is computed

1. Take the time of the track's `first_seen` event.
2. Subtract it from the time of the event: whole seconds for an event at a
   report, a fraction for an interpolated event.
3. An event earlier than `first_seen` gets no value.

## Based on

Developed for OPDI.

## What is published

Column `time_passed_s` of the flight events file, on every event that has a
value.

## Use cases

- **Time between two events** of one flight: the difference of their
  `time_passed_s`, for example taxi-out from `AOBT` to `ATOT`.
- **Time in a region**: the difference between two consecutive `xing-fir`
  events.

## Limitations

It counts from the first report received, not from the off-block or take-off.
See [Limitations: measurements](../limitations.qmd#lim-measurements).

## Availability and accuracy

Exact by definition: it is the difference of two published times. Not
compared with a reference.
